The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA) Prof. Ransford Gyampo has announced that the Boankra Integrated Logistics Terminal (BILT), popularly known as the Boankra Inland Port, has reached 85 per cent completion.
Speaking at a media engagement in Accra, he said the project is among two strategic logistics infrastructure developments being pursued by the Authority to improve Ghana’s cargo handling capacity and strengthen competitiveness
“The Authority therefore continued the development of strategic logistics infrastructure, including the Akatekyiwa Freight Park, which is approximately 70% complete, and the Boankra Integrated Logistics Terminal – 85% complete,” he said.
He said the projected when completed will be Ghana’s flagship dry port — an inland terminal designed to move cargo away from the congested coastal gateways and closer to shippers in the middle and north of the country.
Covering about 413 acres near Kumasi in the Ashanti Region, the Boankra Inland Port will serve as a dry port, allowing importers and exporters outside the coastal capital to clear goods closer to their final destinations, thereby driving regional economic development and job creation.
The multi-million dollar terminal is designed to serve as a major inland logistics hub linking the Tema and Takoradi seaports to Ghana’s middle and northern regions, as well as to landlocked neighbours including Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger.
Prof. Gyampo said delays from excessive border formalities, multiple checkpoints and poor coordination increase vehicle operating costs, demurrage charges and cargo deterioration — and weaken Ghana’s competitiveness as a regional transit hub.
“Ultimately, we want to see a shipping and logistics industry in which charges are transparent and reasonable, service standards are upheld, complaints are addressed promptly, regulatory requirements are respected and Ghanaian businesses can import and export competitively.”
